CB The Story Behind the Stories – Script






Claire in Studio
For our next story we thought we would offer something from left field – in keeping with what is sure to be another unpredictable year in our country.

We’re taking you on a journey, offering a rarely seen insight into the world beyond this studio set…
Claire walking off set
So I'm stepping off set with my cameraman Kobus, to go behind the scenes.
Claire UPS
Thanks so much guys.
Bye Claire!
Claire walking down passage
The show you're watching right now has been months in the making. And just so you know, this little part was originally my idea.
Claire Dressingroom
A whole team of people is involved in some way or another, from original concepts to what you see on Sunday night.
Lourensa
And there's a lot that happens behind the scenes that you don't see.

Sometimes things do go wrong, like just when you think you've nailed that link and a hadeda makes a noise!


Claire
I don't know, I'm supposed to say, oh, but, that's the point…
Oh I should have learnt that line.
Producer
I think that's perfect. Cut it right there. I'm going to use it just like that.
That’s my take.
Govan & Mac UPS
Good evening. This is Carte Blanche.
Masa UPS
Staying close to the wall
Graham
I'm Graham Coetzer, been producing for Carte Blanche, I think, for the last nearly 15 years.
Masa UPS
I can't even see the bottom.
Graham
For me, it was a year of, of organized crime…
INSERT
Entering an abandoned mine shaft controlled by armed zama-zamas is risky.

I feel like I should say bye bye to the real world.
Graham
It's a lot of of planning. I like to know who we're going with. I like the presenter to know that we are as safe as can be.
Masa
I wasn't scared in the moment. I was scared once we got to the zama-zama mountain that they've, you know, taken over, where they had allowed us now in. And then the one zama says to me… Don't be scared, mama. I’m like I wasn't scared until you said that!
Graham
Things can go wrong and have gone wrong in the past very quickly. But to me, it's about speaking to them about what they're willing to do. And our presenters are fantastic. They are just more than happy to try anything.
UPS MAC
Was that in?
That was out!
UPS Govan
We’re in the bomb shelter.
UPS MAC
One hand. One hand!
UPS Claire
This is not instagram.
Govan
I actually didn't think about jumping off the plane until they opened the door.
Lourensa
I did get that call. And I immediately every, every part of my body just froze. Now that I look at that instead and I see the fun that Gavin had. I actually think it's perfect that he got to cover that story, because I think if I did that story, I would have been crying throughout.
Govan
The skydiving was the reward for the hike, but the hike was top tier experience.
UPS Govan
Essentially, we're going up that mountain.
Liz Fish
I’m Liz Fish and I'm a producer, and, I've been a producer for 17 years.

We had to climb a mountain in 40 degrees heat. The cameraman was very willing, but halfway up decided he was going to… and I was relieved because it was an extreme day. So I shot it on a GoPro.


Govan
four and a half hours up and three hours down, and Liz Fish didn't tell me how good she was at climbing mountains.
UPS Govan
This little dip should help us with the weather. I'm feeling refreshed. Almost died at the start of this.
Govan
And I just opened my shirt, stomach out. Pen uit. And Liz Fish is shouting the whole time; “Button up your shirt and tuck it in. We need to shoot some links.”


UPS Govan
Ready? Welcome to a wingsuit pilot’s playground.
UPS Claire
Brutally attacked during one of his training…
UPS Claire
I’m fighting with my shirt!
Erin
You're fighting with the elements. You're trying to walk in a natural way, but suddenly you're self-conscious because there's a camera on you. You're trying to be word perfect, but also relatable in your delivery.


UPS Erin
Senior leaders seemed to be in shock. La la la la la. No.
UPS masa
We wanted to ask jean du Plessis, or anyone at SKG about their…

Thank you for that. That’s lovely.We appreciate it.


UPS Lourensa
And they refer to these illegal connections….
UPS Lourensa
And he fought back about nine km.
UPS Claire
Death by the taxi rank coming alive behind me.

And it looks so cool.
UPS Govan
And it's so bad that a resident had to use his own money to build this barricade, because they didn't want to let the fancy cars drive through the Shit.
UPS Govan
Maybe. What?
No, it’s gonna come and hoot.
Govan
Or they come past… Hey Carte Blanche! Hoezit

Or we’re busy shooting a link and the guys stops: “Are you filming here? Are you guys doing a story?”
UPS Govan
Toe sy die Springbokke ontmoet…

(Swearing)

That’s going on the cut, hey.

Sorry Stenette


Tarryn
I’m Tarryn Crossman and I'm a producer for Carte Blanche.

I'd been walking on the beach in Nahoon, and I was filming on my phone. And I heard these women, like, laughing, and it was, like, contagious laughter. So I filmed it on my phone, and then I sent it to the editorial team. I was like, guys, I need to do the story. And they were like, yeah, put it on a long finger.
INSERT UPS
​​So I switched out my Jozi gear for a wetsuit and borrowed a boogie board.
Lourensa
Every now and again, you get an opportunity to do something that's just out of left field. And so much fun. When I got the call that morning, that we would be hitting the waves with this bunch of, ladies. Amazing woman. It was just the most fun I think I've had on a shoot.
Tarryn
And she was, like, in the waves. And we were in the waves with the GoPros, and we all sat and drank like cappuccinos on the beach. We were like human beings. We ate food and we drank coffee as opposed to like, pah-pah-pah!
UPS Kobus
We don’t want to see happy people at Carte Blanche - this is a tough job! Serious job.
Chwayitisa
My name is Chwayitisa Futshane. I am the managing editor of Carte Blanche.

There's an entire team of producers, of camera, of editors, that are making the machine work.
UPS Claire
Ten rand.
Claire
To sync sound and cameras, because we've got lots of cameras. And so I must make sure that every camera can see me. Cameras are rolling, sound is rolling, and we can sync it all to this moment.
Claire
If I was just doing it once a day, it would be fine. But I have to do it multiple times a day for multiple takes. And people just assume that I'm happy to do a clip. And I didn't even know that. You can have a good clap or a bad clap.


UPS Kobus
Give us a clappy
UPS Claire
It's five rand a clap. Oh, so I forgot to tell you.
Claire
I've told people that they must pay me five rand for every clap I do. I think it's only fair.


UPS
Link, take two.

Oh you’re on a budget, I see.
UPS John
Thank you for being here. This will be the last staff meeting of the year.
John Webb
I'm John Webb, executive producer of Carte Blanche.

I always enjoy the investigative pieces because I think that is where we are at our most impactful, where the show is at its most meaningful.
UPS
I like your beard, man…
John Webb
because we can almost measure the consequence of those stories in the feedback that we get and hopefully the accountability that that follows.
UPS INSERT
Just a month after our story two HPCSA officials were suspended for their involvement in the registration of the American Doctor…
Erin
A story where I really felt on the shoot, this matters, and this is having an impact… was the story I did with producer Liz Fish on the cyberattack on the National Health Laboratory Service.
Govan
It was a breakthrough year for us in a big way, where we touched a lot of areas that we didn't touch before, and we did a lot of dangerous stuff.
UPS INSERT
There's one person on foot coming to us behind a tree. Duck! Someone behind us with a torch. Stay down.
Govan
At one point, we were getting down and we could see that they were around us. And, Thomas Pretorius, the camera guy, is getting down with the cameras on his lap, and he's saying, I can't get down. I'm pulling my hamstring. And Tarryn is next to me. She's in the driver's seat.
I'm in the passenger seat. She says, I'm going to start the car. We say, no, don't do that. And we're getting down. I'm sliding onto the floor with my head popping up, but I can see that there's there's a flash light coming, and I thought that I was going to die.


UPS INSERT
Okay, that was tense. For a moment. We thought that the kidnappers spotters had found us.
Govan
I don't look at my children the same when I do stories about child gangsters. I don't look at myself the same when I go into my hometown to do a kidnapping story. But I feel like I'm evolving, and I feel like I…. That's the best I can offer.
UPS INSERT
A conversation as unsettling as it is deeply uncomfortable.
Claire
You need to go in with no judgment. Ask the questions and try and get the truth. That's the job. That's the gig.


MAsa UPS
When you think of Johannesburg CBD, you probably not thinking about books.
Masa
I love that story because it's going to dispel many people's stereotypes as it did mine. But also, I'm Joe because I was born and bred here. I went to nursery school in Hillbrow in the 80s, so to be in town and celebrating the Johannesburg CBD for literature. On top of that, I think it's a beautiful story, and a lot of the times people say to us, oh, you do such negative stories like you're so depressing. And I say, wait till the last piece. You know, the last piece is always like, you know, your sweet after your medicine.


Masa UPS
I've always wanted to do this. My beauty and the beast moment.

Oh, wow. This looks like a book that came out of beauty and the beast.

Cancer research!


Masa
And. I really hope it's a more peaceful year
Claire
For 2025 I hope that the stories we tell have a lasting impact and effect positive change.
Govan
I want more experiences, more locations, more engaging with South African people.
John Web
It's our ambition to ensure that we move, you know, into 40 years and beyond. So in order to continue doing that, we need to refine, we need to polish, and we need to ensure that we continue to adapt. And that's the program. That's the ambition, that's the vision.










PROMO 1
Claire - I charge R5 for every clap
Clap clap clap
Claire - I have to clap ten thousand times a day
Camera man claps for her
Claire - budget cuts I see


PROMO 2
The highs…

The lows…

And the outrageous…
PROMO 3
VO: An exhilarating year….

VO: Told through thousands of takes and retakes….

VO: It’s the story behind our stories.
